note: Saturday 07:00 SGT weekend sweep, pre-Asia-open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Fri 24 Jul US close — levels/quotes are as of that close unless noted. The dominant cross-portfolio driver stays the escalating US-Iran war, but it BIFURCATES the book: bullish gold/oil, bearish everything rate-sensitive (levered silver, S-REITs, crypto) as markets shifted from pricing a 2026 cut to a possible HIKE. Oil topped $100 mid-week then reversed ~4% Friday on Pakistan/China-brokered de-escalation talk; silver broke below $58. Fresh items (7 of 14) are dated Thu 23–Sat 25 Jul; the rest are decision-relevant items from 15-22 Jul. Every item source-verified against the cited pages.

items.headline: Silver breaks below $58 (~$57.64, -3.5%) as oil-driven inflation revives rate-hike bets
items.summary: Silver fell more than 3% Thursday and traded ~$57.64 Friday (Sep futures opened ~$57.92) as surging oil strengthened the case for tighter Fed policy and lifted real yields (10Y ~4.71%) and the dollar (DXY ~101.5). Non-yielding metals were pressured despite the geopolitical risk; silver remains far more sensitive to the rate-hike narrative than gold and is down from the ~$60 it held earlier in the week.
items.actionable: The levered silver core is the portfolio's biggest short-term vulnerability — an oil-led rate-hike repricing hits silver harder than gold. Treat the break below $58 as a place to trim leverage or hedge the silver-vs-gold spread into the 28-29 Jul FOMC rather than add; a genuine Iran de-escalation is the fastest catalyst to relieve it.

items.headline: US-Iran war escalates; oil topped $100 as Trump weighs a 'massive attack'
items.summary: US Central Command carried out a 13th consecutive night of strikes on Iran; Trump said he was close to deciding on 'a massive attack' and threatened to hold Tehran responsible for Houthi Red Sea attacks. Brent crossed $100/bbl for the first time in ~2 months as Houthi strikes spread maritime risk from the Strait of Hormuz to the Bab al-Mandab. UN Secretary-General Guterres warned the situation is 'getting out of control.'
items.actionable: The single event driving every cross-current in the book: bullish gold/oil and Seatrium's offshore-order backdrop, but the inflation impulse keeps the Fed and MAS hawkish — a headwind for levered silver, S-REITs and HK tech. Watch the binary this weekend: a Hormuz closure (gold+oil tail-risk spike) vs the Pakistan/China-brokered de-escalation talks (unwinds the whole rate-sensitive trade).

items.headline: Fed seen on hold 28-29 Jul, but markets now price a possible 2026 rate HIKE on oil
items.summary: The Fed (chaired by Kevin Warsh since Powell's term ended May 2026) is expected to hold at 3.50-3.75% at its 28-29 July meeting, but oil topping $100 has pushed investors to sharply raise bets on a rate hike later in 2026 rather than the previously-penciled single cut. June CPI cooled to 3.5% headline / 2.6% core, but energy (+15.7% YoY) keeps the Fed cautious; September is flagged as the first real test of durable disinflation.
items.actionable: The shift from 'one cut' to 'possible hike' is the core near-term threat to levered silver and SGX REITs, keeping rates higher-for-longer. The big USD cash pile (earning ~3.5-3.75%) is an asset here — stay patient and let the oil/rate shock resolve before redeploying into rate-sensitive names; a dovish 29 Jul surprise is the upside catalyst.

items.headline: Gold holds ~$4,050 after a $4,130 two-week high as safe-haven demand fights inflation crosscurrents
items.summary: Gold hit a two-week high near $4,130 on 22 July on Iran-war safe-haven bids and a softer dollar, then eased to ~$4,048 by 24 July as oil-driven inflation fears and higher yields (10Y ~4.71%) capped it. Dip-buying persisted around $4,050 and softer US labor data cushioned the downside, though BofA continues to flag a gold 'death cross' and elevated net-longs into the Fed.
items.actionable: Gold is holding up far better than silver in this regime — favor the gold-heavy miners (GDX) over pure silver leverage while the war/inflation tug-of-war persists. The ~$4,130 high is the level to reclaim; a hawkish Fed or Iran de-escalation could fade it toward $4,000.

items.headline: Oil reverses ~4% Friday on Pakistan/China-brokered US-Iran talks hopes
items.summary: Brent fell ~4% to near $97-98 Friday (its biggest one-day drop since late June) after reports that Pakistan, with Chinese support, was seeking to revive US-Iran negotiations; WTI eased toward ~$88. Despite the drop Brent stayed up >12% on the week and WTI ~+10%, with crude still traversing Middle East routes despite the escalation.
items.actionable: Watch this diplomatic thread closely — it's the fastest catalyst to unwind the rate-hike fear and let levered silver, SGX REITs and crypto rebound. A relief in oil is bearish the energy long but a tailwind for the far-larger rate-sensitive book; trade the de-escalation odds, not the individual legs.

items.headline: Hong Kong tech rallies; Hang Seng reclaims 25,000 on policy/flows/earnings 'triple-bottom'
items.summary: The Hang Seng Index surged ~600 points to reclaim 25,000, with the Hang Seng Tech Index up ~2.8%. Tencent gained 3.5%; Xiaomi, Meituan and JD each rose >3%; SMIC and Alibaba also contributed. Drivers cited: a 'triple-bottom' of supportive policy, capital inflows and an earnings recovery — though AI-application names diverged sharply.
items.actionable: Momentum and flows favor the HK-tech core (Tencent, SMIC, Xiaomi) into earnings season — hold, but the rally now hinges on late-July Politburo follow-through not disappointing. Favor Tencent on relative strength (AI traction + buybacks).

items.headline: China Q2 GDP misses at 4.3% (weakest in 3+ years); late-July Politburo in focus
items.summary: China's Q2 GDP grew 4.3% YoY, below the 4.5% forecast and down from 5.0% in Q1 — the weakest in over three years — with H1 urban fixed-asset investment falling 5.7%. Investors are watching the late-July Politburo meeting for stimulus signals, though analysts expect no aggressive action given resilient exports and anti-deflation capacity discipline.
items.actionable: The late-July Politburo is a binary catalyst for the HK-tech holdings — position for a measured, no-bazooka outcome; a disappointment could stall the recent Hang Seng Tech rally, while a forceful property/demand backstop would spark a sharp large-cap rebound.

items.headline: Lynas posts record quarterly revenue A$288.9m; signs JS Link magnet JV in Malaysia
items.summary: Lynas reported record quarterly revenue of A$288.9m for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 on heavy-rare-earth expansion (though shy of ~A$391m consensus), with a strong A$1.21bn cash position. It also signed a long-term partnership with JS Link to build a rare-earth permanent-magnet plant near its Kuantan, Malaysia facility, extending mine-to-magnet integration.
items.actionable: Lynas is executing on mine-to-magnet integration and printing record cash — a top ex-China watchlist candidate if converting some of the cash pile into the rare-earth theme; not on China's control list, unlike MP/USAR. A record top-line but a consensus miss means the entry is on weakness, not chasing.

items.headline: China rare-earth export controls suspended to 10 Nov; magnet exports hit a 6-month high
items.summary: China has suspended (until 10 Nov 2026) the Oct-2025 export controls following the Xi-Trump rollback deal, and rare-earth magnet exports jumped to a six-month high of 5,577 tonnes (+75% MoM); US shipments rose 75.5% to 619 tonnes but remain below pre-restriction levels. New Western magnet capacity is due online in summer 2026.
items.actionable: Eased Chinese supply is a short-term headwind to rare-earth pricing/urgency — the ex-China names are a strategic optionality play on the controls snapping back after 10 Nov, not an immediate momentum trade. Accumulate on weakness into that catalyst.

items.headline: MP Materials' DoD deal cements a US domestic magnet supply chain with a price floor
items.summary: MP Materials secured a landmark US Department of Defense partnership (DoD ~15% stake, ~$400M preferred + warrants, a 10-year 7,000 t/yr magnet offtake at a $110/kg NdPr price floor) to fast-track a fully integrated domestic rare-earth magnet supply chain — a structural shift in US critical-minerals policy that provides offtake/price support insulated from Chinese swings. Apple added a $500M magnet/recycling partnership.
items.actionable: The DoD backstop and $110/kg floor make MP the highest-conviction US rare-earth name on the watchlist and de-risk the whole Western complex — favor it (and government-backed UUUU) over pure-China-exposed peers on China-retaliation dips.

items.headline: Singapore STI at record highs; DBS/OCBC/UOB peak, earnings season starts
items.summary: The STI hit a record ~5,561 on 15 July (about +21% total return YTD through 17 July) before easing to ~5,509, driven by safe-haven flows, MAS reforms and attractive yields. DBS, OCBC and UOB all hit record highs (OCBC leading on wealth/non-interest income). Key dates ahead: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug, DBS 6 Aug.
items.actionable: SGX banks are riding record highs into 6 Aug DBS earnings — a supportive backdrop for the blue-chip sleeve. But if the oil-led rate-hike narrative sticks, the REIT holdings (Keppel REIT, Mapletree PACT) are more exposed than the banks; watch the yield backdrop and the end-July MAS review.

items.headline: Bitcoin drops to ~$65k, Ether ~$1,880 as oil-driven yields hit risk assets
items.summary: Bitcoin opened ~$65,048 (-1.6%) and Ethereum ~$1,877 (-2.9%) Friday as higher oil, tariff-driven inflation expectations and rising US Treasury yields pulled institutional money out of risk assets. Crypto is trading purely off the macro rate/yield channel this week, with the alternative.me Fear & Greed at 28 (Fear).
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is moving in lockstep with the silver/REIT rate-sensitivity trade — the same Iran de-escalation catalyst that would help silver would relieve crypto. Treat it as a risk-appetite barometer; there is no crypto-specific bullish driver right now.

items.headline: EU adopts 21st Russia sanctions package — largest in 4 years, targets crypto rails
items.summary: The EU Council adopted its 21st Russia sanctions package — 218 listings (48 individuals, 170 entities), the largest batch in four years — targeting energy, banks, the shadow fleet and crypto. It bans transactions with 14 offshore crypto platforms (incl. HTX/Justin Sun) and creates authority to blanket-ban crypto services from entire third countries facilitating sanctions evasion. Rubio met Lavrov on 23 July on ASEAN sidelines in Manila.
items.actionable: A structural tightening of offshore crypto rails adds regulatory overhang to the crypto sleeve — a reason to keep crypto exposure modest versus the metals core; low direct relevance beyond that.

items.headline: Russia-Ukraine: strikes continue as US-Russia diplomacy stays open
items.summary: Ukraine struck targets across Russia early 24 July (including Wildberries warehouses) while Russian air attacks killed at least 15 in Ukraine; diplomatic channels remain open after the Rubio-Lavrov meeting. The EU's new sanctions package reflects a compromise balancing pressure on Russia with protecting EU economic interests.
items.actionable: A secondary, slow-burn geopolitical support for the gold sleeve — lower decision-relevance than the Iran war, but an additional safe-haven tailwind to keep on the radar.
